svg.aria-label: Telling oriental arborvitae, Chinese juniper and savin juniper apart (schematic). Oriental arborvitae (Platycladus orientalis, source of Cebaiye) is an evergreen upright tree; its twigs are flat and arranged in one upright plane, like a hand held edgeways; all its leaves are tiny and scale-like, in opposite pairs, pressed close to the twigs; the cones are ovoid with 4 pairs of cone scales, each with a curved-back point at the top of its back, splitting open when ripe. Chinese juniper (Yuanbai) often has two kinds of leaf, needle-like and scale-like, on the same plant; its twigs are not arranged in a plane, and its cones are fleshy and do not split open; it is not a Pharmacopoeia species. Savin juniper (Shadibai, Juniperus sabina) is a creeping shrub, mostly found on sandy land in the north-west and in landscape planting; the whole plant is poisonous, it contains savin oil and can cause vomiting, liver and kidney damage and miscarriage. Do not pick a cypress that creeps along the ground and whose twigs do not form upright planes; if unsure, do not pick
